title: Latency vs throughput heuristics scratchpad
content:
TL;DR: After the 2025-02-12 runtime deploy we saw a sustained ~30% throughput drop for a subset of customer traffic that uses long-context chat (avg seq len 1800). Root cause likely interaction between continuous-batcher prefill heuristic + new slot allocation code that reduces active batch windows when prefill success rate dips. This doc is a lab scratchpad with commands I ran, error snippets, metric snapshots, quick experiments, hypotheses and next steps.

Observations / timeline:
- 2025-02-12 03:10 UTC: deploy v7.4.1 (release notes: slot-allocation-rework, prefill-fallbacks). Canary passed.
- 2025-02-12 04:42 UTC: first alerts - dedicated-nyc-prod queue latency SLOs violated for model-phi-3b-long.
- 2025-02-12 05:00-08:00 UTC: sustained throughput drop for long-context routes: QPS 1200 -> 820 (-32%). Short-context routes unaffected.
- 2025-02-12 06:15 UTC: rollback to v7.4.0 partial; throughput recovered by ~20% but not fully.

Quick metric snapshots (from console /prom queries):
- route: chat-long-context-prod (2025-02-12 04:30 -> 06:00)
  - avg QPS: 1183 -> 795
  - p50 latency (tokens): 18ms -> 26ms
  - p95 latency (tokens): 72ms -> 140ms
  - batch fill factor: 0.68 -> 0.44
  - prefill success rate: 0.92 -> 0.57

Commands I ran (notes inline):
- kubectl logs -n serving deploy/continuous-batcher -c cbatch --since=3h | grep "prefill" | tail -n 200  (saw repeated: "prefill attempt timed out after 120ms")
- curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" "https://internal-admin/api/v1/slots/inspect?model=model-phi-3b-long" | jq '.'  (returned slot allocations per node; average active_windows_per_slot down by ~30%)
- git checkout HEAD~1 && git diff -- stat (inspected slot allocation rework commit; noticed change to max_active_windows default)
- go test ./pkg/batcher -run TestPrefillBackpressure -v (local unit reproducer failed intermittently: race between prefill fallback path and batch window shrink)
- pprof http://cbatcher-prod:6060/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=30 -- shows increased time in kvcache.Resolve and in batchWindowManager.scan

Error snippets / logs captured:
- "prefill: resolved 0 prefixes, falling back to cold path. window_shrink=true"
- "assertion failed: window_count >= 1 (was 0)" from batch_window_manager.go:184
- "prefill attempt timed out after 120ms (deadline=100ms)" repeated 420x in 10m window
- "slot-allocator: decreased active_windows for slot s-3f to 1 (reason=conservative-fill-delta)"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Prefill timeout threshold change + slot allocation conservative heuristic caused persistent under-provisioning of active windows for long-context requests. Because those requests need larger KV warmups, reduced windows mean less concurrent prefill attempts and batching degenerates (low fill factor).
2) New slot-allocation code contains a race where, under transient prefill failures, it permanently tags slots as "low-confidence" and they don't recover until manual reset or long cooldown. This explains partial recovery after rollback.
3) Batch-window shrink logic reads stale telemetry due to metric aggregation TTL (60s) causing oscillation; when prefill fails the shrink is aggressive and prevents subsequent fills from succeeding.
4) Less likely: quantization fallback path introduced regressions in token sampling causing longer decoding time per token, but profiling points more to batching/kv work.

Experiments attempted (and outcomes):
- Experiment A: increase prefill timeout from 100ms -> 300ms on a single canary pod (k8s patch) and observe fill factor. Result: prefill success rate jumped 0.58 -> 0.85 on that pod, fill factor recovered to ~0.7, inferred that many prefill failures were latency timeouts not logic errors.
- Experiment B: temporarily set max_active_windows=8 (was 4) for a node pool. Result: throughput recovered ~28% for that pool, but CPU jumped; suggests more concurrency helps but must be bounded.
- Experiment C: forced slot cooldown reset endpoint (/admin/slots/reset?s=...) on one node; slot recovered but other nodes still low. Partial support for hypothesis 2.

Local reproducer notes:
- Reproducer uses loadgen with seq len distribution {short:0.6, long:0.4} and interarrival modeled from prod traces. Under simulated prefill latency of 120ms, batcher exhibited wobble: alternating high fill, then rapid shrink. Adding jitter to prefill backoff mitigates steady-state oscillation.

Open leads / next steps (short checklist):
- [ ] Add temporary increase to prefill timeout for critical long-context routes behind feature flag.
- [ ] Add a fast rollback toggle to slot-allocator to avoid long cooldowns (admin endpoint already exists, but add auto-detect and quick-revert path).
- [ ] Instrument slot-allocator decisions in more detail (emit why= tag and last_success_ts) — open PR to emit structured tags (github PR linked in metadata).
- [ ] Run a canary with max_active_windows bumped to 6 and CPU limits adjusted; monitor cost delta vs throughput.
- [ ] Add e2e test that simulates prefill latency to catch regressions in future slot-allocator changes.
- [ ] Short-term: revert conservative-fill-delta default to previous value (config change), coordinate with SRE for midnight deploy window.

Notes to self / random thoughts:
- This feels like a classic control-loop oscillation with asymmetric treatment of failure (punitive shrink, slow recovery). Try soft-fail strategy: allow N consecutive prefill failures before shrinking window.
- Consider moving prefill on critical routes to optimistic background warmup (best-effort) rather than gating active windows. Could save headroom.
- If we increase timeouts, need to watch p50 token latency impact; might increase tail latency for short requests when concurrency saturated.

Quick references I used during debugging:
- Slack thread with customer: slack://thread/C02CUSTOM/1678880000.123456
- GitHub PR (in metadata): github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/872
- Jira for incident: JIRA-CRIT-1243

If I don't finish: handoff to Marco (cc Elena). Marco, start with the canary change (prefill timeout) and coordinate SRE for a node pool config change. Record all experiments as comments in the Jira ticket.

End of scratchpad. Will prune and formalize once hypothesis validated.
